content: Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark. While Denmark maintains control over foreign affairs, defense, and monetary policy, Greenland has substantial self-governance. The island has its own parliament (Inatsisartut) and government (Naalakkersuisut), with the ability to make decisions on most local matters. In 2009, Greenland was granted even greater autonomy through the Act on Greenland Self-Rule. However, Denmark still provides significant financial support to Greenland, and the Danish monarch remains the head of state.
